findings.issue: A brand-new page (/team) with a new table and interaction was shipped without ever being viewed in a browser; verification was the acceptance suite only, and the agent explicitly reasoned 'tests cover' instead of confirming.
findings.suggestion: After the suite passes, render the new page headlessly (agent-browser/Playwright screenshot) and eyeball layout against the app's existing pages, especially since no reference screenshot exists for /team.

findings.issue: Removing a member re-fetches the entire page HTML and DOM-replaces #team-content via DOMParser — heavyweight and re-runs scripts implicitly, for what is a one-item list change.
findings.suggestion: Either do a plain location.reload(), or render the team list from a small client fetch of just the member data; keep the update proportional to the change.

findings.issue: readTeam/writeTeam and TEAM_SIZE are duplicated between this inline script and the one in team.astro (app/src/pages/team.astro:81-88), drifting from the exported constants in app/src/lib/team.ts.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared client module (e.g. app/src/lib/team-client.ts) exporting readTeam/writeTeam and TEAM_SIZE, and import it from both scripts.

findings.issue: The cookie is written with raw, unencoded values (no encodeURIComponent) and no conservative attributes beyond Path/Max-Age/SameSite.
findings.suggestion: encodeURIComponent the value on write and decode on read; harmless for current API names but cheap insurance against future data.

findings.issue: New TypeScript added but `astro check` was never run (0 typechecks in measured facts), even though the codebase has a tsconfig.
findings.suggestion: Run `astro check` (or `tsc --noEmit`) once before declaring done.

summary: An exceptionally clean run: the agent read everything relevant first, made the one genuinely tricky decision (cookie-backed SSR state) deliberately and correctly in a single pass, and landed the whole feature with zero failed tool calls and a first-run 63/63 test pass. The only real gap is that verification never went beyond the acceptance suite — no browser look at the new /team page, no typecheck. Nothing was wasted; nothing was debugged because nothing broke.
